question: What is the main job of the Leydig cells found in the testes?

options.A: Protecting developing germ cells from immune attack
options.B: Providing nutritional support to immature spermatids
options.C: Transporting mature sperm out of the lobules
options.D: Producing and secreting the hormone testosterone

explanation: You're doing great! Leydig cells hang out right between the sperm-producing tubes and are responsible for pumping out testosterone, the key male hormone. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which body problem is a very common cause of sudden confusion or unconsciousness?

options.A: Severe hypoglycemia
options.B: A ruptured cerebral aneurysm
options.C: Bacterial meningitis
options.D: A penetrating skull fracture

explanation: Spot on! When blood sugar drops too low (hypoglycemia), the brain gets starved of its main energy source and shuts down fast. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h3)

question: Which kitchen habit helps prevent accidental grease or boiling water spills?

options.A: Using metal spoons for all cooking tasks
options.B: Turning pot handles inward toward the stove back
options.C: Leaving burners on high heat while cleaning
options.D: Placing hot oil pans near the edge of the counter

explanation: Turning handles inward keeps pots out of reach of children and prevents adults from accidentally bumping into them. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h4)

question: Why do we take a musculoskeletal history before doing a physical exam on a patient?

options.A: To measure the patient's exact bone density accurately
options.B: To provide context for interpreting physical findings safely
options.C: To replace the need for diagnostic blood tests entirely
options.D: To determine the exact surgical procedure required

explanation: Gathering a thorough history first gives you the background story you need to understand what you find during the physical exam. Great job! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T2#GNS222_U1_T2_h1)

question: If you notice that a broken borehole is causing waterborne illnesses, what role are you mainly playing?

options.A: Hospital administrator
options.B: Surgical assistant
options.C: Needs assessor
options.D: Pharmacist

explanation: Spot on! Spotting a health issue and tracing it back to environmental problems is what a needs assessment is all about. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h4)

question: Why do some religious groups advise against using artificial contraceptives?

options.A: They think it causes instant weight gain
options.B: They view it as interference with divine creation
options.C: They believe it lowers local school fees
options.D: They require proof of modern education first

explanation: Exactly! Certain faiths teach that life is solely in divine hands, leading them to view artificial birth control as interfering with creation. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T006#GNS226_U6_T006_h3)

question: What is the normal resting respiratory rate for a healthy adult?

options.A: 8 to 11 breaths per minute
options.B: 22 to 30 breaths per minute
options.C: 12 to 20 breaths per minute
options.D: 35 to 40 breaths per minute

explanation: A normal, healthy adult at rest breathes between 12 and 20 times every minute. Rates outside this range can indicate underlying respiratory or metabolic problems. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h1)

question: In a busy hospital, what percentage of the total waste produced is actually regular, non-hazardous household waste?

options.A: About 50%
options.B: About 99%
options.C: About 15%
options.D: About 85%

explanation: Most of what hospitals throw away is everyday rubbish (like paper and food packaging) that doesn't carry any infection risks. Only a small fraction is dangerous clinical waste! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h1)

question: Why is reproductive health nursing considered a sensitive area of care?

options.A: It involves more paperwork than other clinical departments
options.B: It deals with deeply personal aspects tied to self-image and culture
options.C: Medical treatments for these conditions are always experimental
options.D: Patients are rarely willing to talk about their symptoms

explanation: Exactly! Reproductive health touches on private parts of life, culture, and identity. Showing extra empathy and privacy goes a long way. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T14#GNS311_U1_T14_h1)

question: Why is patting the perineal skin dry just as important as washing it?

options.A: Wet skin makes it impossible to apply a clean hospital gown
options.B: Leaving moisture behind fosters bacterial growth and skin breakdown
options.C: Rough rubbing removes the patient's natural body hair
options.D: Moisture attracts insects into the hospital room

explanation: Germs love warm, wet places. Taking that extra second to pat the area completely dry is a simple step that keeps skin strong and healthy. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T8#GNS112_U5_T8_h5)

question: What type of energy does an MRI machine use to create images of the body?

options.A: Ultraviolet light rays
options.B: High-frequency sound waves
options.C: High doses of ionizing radiation
options.D: Strong magnetic fields and radiofrequency waves

explanation: An MRI does not use harmful radiation like X-rays or CT scans; instead, it uses large magnets and radio waves to take pictures inside the body. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h1)

question: What practical change can nurses advocate for to help more men attend clinics?

options.A: Charging male visitors a special facility fee
options.B: Scheduling weekend or evening clinic hours
options.C: Requiring fathers to wear special uniforms
options.D: Banning all female relatives from the waiting room

explanation: Flexible clinic hours make it possible for men who work during regular weekdays to attend. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T7#GNS312_U4_T7_h7)

question: A patient asks you why he developed gout, considering he loves rich meals and has high blood pressure. How do you explain it simply?

options.A: He has a severe bacterial joint infection passed down through his family
options.B: His kidneys and diet are allowing uric acid to build up crystals in his joints
options.C: His body is manufacturing too many red blood cells instead of white cells
options.D: His blood pressure medication is creating calcium deposits in his bones

explanation: You nailed it! Risk factors like diet, blood pressure, and kidney function team up to let uric acid levels rise, leading to crystal deposits. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h3)

question: Why do doctors order a D-dimer blood test when checking for a deep vein thrombosis (DVT)?

options.A: To look for protein fragments that show a recent blood clot is breaking down
options.B: To measure blood pressure inside leg veins
options.C: To see plaque buildup inside the aorta
options.D: To check how fast red blood cells settle in a tube

explanation: D-dimer is a leftover protein piece that floats around when the body is dissolving a blood clot. If the test is negative, it's a great clue that a clot isn't lurking there! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T10#GNS213_U1_T10_h7)

question: How can nurses actively help prevent unsafe abortions out in the community?

options.A: By educating the public on modern contraception and reproductive health
options.B: By banning the sale of harmful chemicals in local markets
options.C: By arresting individuals who perform illegal medical procedures
options.D: By strictly refusing to treat patients who attempted self-induction

explanation: Exactly right! Community education prevents unintended pregnancies in the first place, reducing the need for dangerous, hidden procedures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h6)

question: What is a major risk of mixing herbal products with HIV medications without asking a doctor?

options.A: They turn the medicine into harmless sugar water
options.B: They always cure the infection faster
options.C: They have zero effect on drugs
options.D: They can dangerously lower drug levels in the blood

explanation: Correct! Some herbs mess with liver enzymes, clearing out life-saving medications too quickly and making them less effective. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T5#GNS216_U6_T5_h6)

question: What is the main difference between droplet and airborne germs?

options.A: Airborne germs only spread outdoors
options.B: Airborne germs cannot infect healthcare workers
options.C: Droplet germs need negative pressure rooms
options.D: Droplet germs travel on heavy particles that fall quickly, while airborne germs stay floating longer

explanation: Think of it by weight! Heavier droplets drop fast to the ground, but tiny airborne particles float around longer and need stronger masks. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h1)

question: Which formula is used to calculate cardiac output?

options.A: Blood pressure divided by resistance
options.B: Stroke volume multiplied by heart rate
options.C: Stroke volume plus blood volume
options.D: Heart rate divided by stroke volume

explanation: Cardiac output is the product of how much blood is pumped per beat (stroke volume) and how many beats occur per minute (heart rate). [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why should a nurse teach a patient with diabetic foot neuropathy to test bathwater with their elbow instead of their feet?

options.A: Numbness in the feet prevents the patient from accurately sensing water temperature, risking scald burns
options.B: Elbow skin contains specialized sweat glands that neutralize toxic minerals found in tap water
options.C: Hot water causes immediate and permanent paralysis of the small motor nerves in the toes
options.D: The skin on the feet is biologically incapable of absorbing heat evenly compared to the upper body

explanation: Because neuropathy takes away normal feeling in the feet, patients might step into water that's way too hot without realizing it until they get burned. Using the elbow helps keep them safe! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h7)

question: Why is it so important to figure out the exact type of prostatitis a patient has?

options.A: It indicates that immediate surgical removal of the prostate is needed
options.B: It prevents the future development of benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.C: It proves whether the patient has concurrent testicular cancer
options.D: It dictates whether antibiotics or non-infectious management is required

explanation: Brilliant! Bacterial infections need antibiotics, while other types of pelvic pain need a totally different, non-infectious treatment plan. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h3)

question: Why do teenagers often take big risks even when they know it's dangerous?

options.A: They experience a permanent loss of short-term memory
options.B: They completely lack the ability to think logically
options.C: Their cognitive development stops entirely during puberty
options.D: Reward-seeking brain centers develop faster than impulse-control centers

explanation: The thrill-seeking part of the brain develops faster than the brake pedal (impulse control), making exciting experiences feel totally worth the risk to them. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T4#GNS312_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why might a financially dependent housewife hesitate to disclose her HIV status to her husband?

options.A: She fears losing her financial support and home if he reacts with anger or abandonment
options.B: She knows her husband already takes antiretroviral medications secretly
options.C: She is legally prohibited from speaking to her spouse about medical issues
options.D: She believes her husband will automatically cure the virus with traditional herbs

explanation: Economic vulnerability heavily complicates disclosure because patients worry about survival if rejection leads to destitution. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h5)

question: Why should a nurse refer to the National Health Act when talking to health authorities about changes?

options.A: It exempts the nurse from paying professional licensing taxes
options.B: It gives legal backing and strength to the nurse's advocacy demands
options.C: It prevents patients from filing lawsuits against nurses
options.D: It allows the nurse to take over the duties of the hospital director

explanation: Exactly! Backing your points up with official health laws turns a simple complaint into a serious, legal expectation that administrators can't easily brush aside. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h6)

question: A patient has a sudden blockage in a main coronary artery. What is the immediate danger to the heart?

options.A: The heart valves will instantly turn inside out from lack of pressure.
options.B: The cardiac conduction system will stop making red blood cells.
options.C: The heart muscle supplied by that artery will be starved of oxygen and may die.
options.D: The lungs will immediately fill with air instead of blood.

explanation: When a coronary artery gets blocked, the heart muscle cells downstream lose their oxygen supply. If it's not fixed quickly, that part of the muscle gets damaged—this is what we call a heart attack. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which complication happens most directly when sharp metal objects are pushed into the uterus?

options.A: Chronic hypertension and peripheral edema
options.B: Uterine perforation and severe hemorrhage
options.C: Allergic rhinitis and skin rashes
options.D: Renal stone formation and bladder spasms

explanation: Unskilled hands using sharp instruments can easily pierce the muscular wall of the uterus, causing heavy internal bleeding. That's a major medical emergency! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of providing quality care in reproductive health?

options.A: Reducing the total number of hospital admissions
options.B: Ensuring services are safe, effective, and respectful
options.C: Lowering the operational costs of the clinic
options.D: Maximizing the daily number of patients seen

explanation: Quality care focuses on delivering safe, effective, and respectful services that build client trust and promote positive health outcomes. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h1)

question: How does skeletal traction differ fundamentally from skin traction?

options.A: Skeletal traction avoids any risk of infection because no hardware is used
options.B: Skeletal traction uses much lighter weights for short periods
options.C: Skeletal traction attaches directly to bone using metal pins
options.D: Skeletal traction relies entirely on elastic bandages wrapped loosely

explanation: Skeletal traction requires surgical insertion of pins or wires into the bone to handle heavier weights over a longer duration, unlike skin-surface methods. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T7#GNS221_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why is it a good idea to soak a patient's nails in warm water before trimming them?

options.A: It softens the hard nail plate and cuticles for easier trimming
options.B: It permanently kills all bacteria hiding under the nail bed
options.C: It stops the patient from feeling any cold drafts in the room
options.D: It opens up the pores so the skin absorbs extra vitamins

explanation: Spot on! Warm water softens up the hard keratin, making clipping smooth and saving your patient from painful splits or cracks. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h4)

question: How does cyanide primarily cause damage inside human cells?

options.A: It binds permanently to calcium channels in cardiac muscle tissue.
options.B: It directly dissolves the lipid bilayer of red blood cells.
options.C: It triggers widespread liquefactive necrosis in the esophagus.
options.D: It inhibits mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase, halting cellular respiration.

explanation: Cyanide attacks the powerhouses of our cells (the mitochondria). By blocking cytochrome c oxidase, cells can no longer use oxygen to make energy, leading to rapid collapse. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h4)

question: Besides checking physical lab results, what else should a nurse assess during routine consultations?

options.A: The patient's emotional readiness and coping style
options.B: The exact brand of clothing the patient prefers
options.C: The patient's long-term career and retirement plans
options.D: The architectural layout of the patient's house

explanation: Comprehensive nursing assessment evaluates mental health and emotional coping alongside physical health parameters. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h5)

question: Which skin sign is most often seen in patients with a low platelet count (thrombocytopenia)?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the skin
options.B: Severe dry and peeling patches
options.C: Petechiae and easy bruising
options.D: Widespread painful blistering

explanation: Without enough platelets to patch tiny leaks in blood vessels, patients easily get tiny red dots (petechiae) and bruises from minor bumps. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T2#GNS311_U2_T2_h4)

question: A patient suddenly feels terrified, has chest pain, and fears they are dying, all within a few minutes. What is happening?

options.A: Panic disorder
options.B: Social anxiety disorder
options.C: Generalized anxiety disorder
options.D: Specific phobia

explanation: These intense, sudden waves of terror are classic panic attacks. Patients often rush to the emergency room genuinely believing they are having a heart attack. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T10#GNS123_U3_T10_h3)

question: What happens when someone gets a transfusion of the wrong, incompatible blood type?

options.A: The recipient's bone marrow stops producing new hemoglobin
options.B: Plasma proteins dissolve all white blood cells in the sample
options.C: Donor red blood cells undergo agglutination and hemolysis
options.D: Platelets instantly multiply to repair the blood vessels

explanation: You nailed it! The recipient's antibodies attack the foreign blood cells, causing them to clump together (agglutinate) and break apart (hemolysis). [learn more](GNS311_U2_T1#GNS311_U2_T1_h7)

question: Which physical sign is commonly seen during the active dying phase?

options.A: Cool, mottled extremities and weak pulses
options.B: Rapid increase in blood pressure and clear speech
options.C: High fever and severe muscle contractions
options.D: Sudden increase in appetite and high energy

explanation: As circulation naturally slows down near the end of life, the hands and feet often feel cool and may look pale or blotchy (mottled). [learn more](GNS321_U4_T4#GNS321_U4_T4_h8)

question: Why do nurses ask about a patient's job or occupation during a health history?

options.A: To calculate their exact daily caloric intake requirements
options.B: To reveal potential exposure to environmental toxins or stress
options.C: To determine their precise health insurance coverage tier
options.D: To predict their exact date of retirement from work

explanation: Great job! A person's daily work environment can play a huge role in health issues, from chemical exposures to heavy stress. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T3#GNS222_U3_T3_h2)

question: A patient arrives with a severe insect sting on their hand, and the hand is swelling up massively. What quick check should you do next?

options.A: Draw blood samples for comprehensive metabolic panels
options.B: Check distal pulses, movement, and sensation in the fingers
options.C: Measure the patient's exact height and weight
options.D: Prepare the patient for immediate surgical amputation

explanation: When a tight space like the hand swells up, blood flow and nerves can get squeezed. Checking fingers for pulses, feeling, and movement helps catch bad circulation early! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h3)

question: Why do patients with chronic glomerulonephritis sometimes notice foamy urine?

options.A: High amounts of sugar
options.B: Too many white blood cells
options.C: Presence of excess protein
options.D: Excessive water intake

explanation: You've got this! When damaged glomeruli let large protein molecules slip through into the urine, it creates bubbles, giving the urine a noticeable foamy look. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T5#GNS213_U4_T5_h4)

question: Between these patients, who is most at risk of developing constipation from slowed body movement?

options.A: A nursing student drinking several cups of coffee daily
options.B: A young athlete who drinks water after a football match
options.C: An older adult on strict bed rest after hip surgery
options.D: A patient with a mild viral stomach flu and loose stools

explanation: Well done! Staying in bed without moving, especially as we grow older, slows down natural bowel activity and makes constipation a major risk. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h2)

question: A patient asks how long an egg can survive and be fertilized after ovulation. What is your best response?

options.A: Up to 5 days
options.B: About 24 hours
options.C: Less than 1 hour
options.D: Exactly 1 week

explanation: Good clinical knowledge to have! An ovulated egg has a short window of about 12 to 24 hours to meet a sperm before it breaks down. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T9#GNS121_U5_T9_h6)

question: Which type of birth control protects against both unplanned pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Hormonal injections
options.B: Intrauterine devices (IUDs)
options.C: Long-acting implants
options.D: Barrier methods

explanation: Condoms and other barrier methods act as a physical shield against both sperm and infections. Simple and effective! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h4)

question: How do deep, slow breathing exercises physically help a patient calm down?

options.A: They increase skeletal muscle tension to release trapped toxins
options.B: They permanently block the adrenal glands from producing cortisol
options.C: They flood the bloodstream with extra adrenaline to burn off energy
options.D: They stimulate the vagus nerve to activate the parasympathetic nervous system

explanation: Deep breathing acts like a brake pedal for your nervous system, stimulating the vagus nerve to switch you from 'fight-or-flight' to 'rest-and-digest.' [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h7)

question: What is a recommended safety item for a patient diagnosed with a chronic seizure disorder to wear at all times?

options.A: A medical alert bracelet
options.B: A portable oxygen tank
options.C: A hard plastic safety helmet
options.D: A bright yellow reflective vest

explanation: A medical alert bracelet provides instant information to bystanders and healthcare workers if the patient has a seizure in public. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h8)

question: On a standard X-ray picture, why do healthy bones show up as bright white?

options.A: Soft tissues completely block all light while bone lets light pass through
options.B: Bones naturally emit a bright fluorescent light when exposed to air
options.C: The radiologist manually paints the bone structures white after the scan
options.D: Dense structures like cortical bone absorb most of the X-ray beams

explanation: Because bones are dense, they block the X-ray beams from passing through to the film. That blockage is what creates that classic bright white look! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T5#GNS222_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is considered the single most effective way to stop the spread of infection?

options.A: Wearing sterile gowns
options.B: Hand hygiene
options.C: Routine room painting
options.D: Using plastic aprons

explanation: Proper handwashing or alcohol rub use removes transient microbes from hands, preventing cross-contamination between patients. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which syringe and needle setup is best for giving a Mantoux skin test?

options.A: A 1-mL tuberculin syringe with a short 27-gauge fine needle
options.B: A 5-mL syringe with a blunt-tip drawing needle
options.C: An insulin syringe marked in units with a permanent attached needle
options.D: A 3-mL syringe with a large 21-gauge intramuscular needle

explanation: You need a tiny syringe to measure tiny drops accurately, and a short, fine needle helps you slide the fluid right into the top layers of the skin! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h3)

question: How many patient identifiers should a nurse check before giving a medication?

options.A: At least two identifiers
options.B: Three separate room numbers
options.C: Four family member approvals
options.D: Only one quick identifier

explanation: Using identifiers like the patient's name and hospital number ensures the right person receives the treatment. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h3)

question: You notice continuous bubbling in the water-seal chamber of a chest tube system. What does this usually mean?

options.A: An expected amount of residual blood loss
options.B: An air leak somewhere in the tubing or insertion site
options.C: Blockage of the chest tube drainage lumen
options.D: Normal lung re-expansion and healing

explanation: While tiny occasional bubbles can be normal, continuous bubbling is like a leaky bicycle tire telling us air is getting in where it shouldn't. Excellent clinical observation! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T7#GNS213_U2_T7_h5)

question: A patient is assessed as a high fall risk. Which nursing action is best to keep them safe?

options.A: Remove all pillows from the bed to reduce soft surface risks
options.B: Ensure the bed is in the lowest position with the call bell close by
options.C: Keep the room lights completely off to encourage deep sleep
options.D: Encourage the patient to walk alone to the bathroom frequently

explanation: Keeping the bed low reduces injury if they fall, and keeping the call bell close means they can easily ask for your help before trying to get up! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T8#GNS122_U3_T8_h6)

question: If your patient is very thin and malnourished, how might you adjust your subcutaneous technique?

options.A: The injection must be given at a 90-degree angle always
options.B: The medication must be diluted with sterile water first
options.C: A longer needle must be used to reach the fat layer
options.D: A shorter needle and a shallower insertion angle may be needed

explanation: Exactly! Thin patients have less fat padding, so using a shorter needle or a 45-degree angle helps make sure you don't accidentally go straight into the muscle. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which medication route involves placing a tablet under the tongue to dissolve?

options.A: Transdermal
options.B: Intradermal
options.C: Subcutaneous
options.D: Sublingual

explanation: Sublingual medications dissolve under the tongue where rich blood vessels allow quick absorption into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do foetal lungs get only a tiny fraction of the body's blood supply?

options.A: They are completely absent during the first two trimesters
options.B: They are blocked by the growing liver tissue
options.C: They are filled with fluid and have high resistance
options.D: They receive all their oxygen directly from the mother's skin

explanation: Uninflated lungs full of amniotic fluid naturally push back against blood flow, so most blood finds easier alternate routes. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h5)

question: What does a high waist circumference mostly tell you about a patient's health risk?

options.A: Severe protein deficiency and muscle wasting
options.B: A normal and healthy distribution of total body water
options.C: Excess visceral fat linked to heart disease and diabetes
options.D: Chronic lung disease and poor oxygen exchange

explanation: Fat stored around the belly and internal organs is strongly linked to a higher risk of heart problems and diabetes. Excellent clinical insight! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T3#GNS112_U6_T3_h5)

question: Which common class of medications is known to raise blood sugar levels over time?

options.A: Antibiotics
options.B: Corticosteroids
options.C: Antihistamines
options.D: Pain relievers

explanation: You got it! Steroids push the liver to make more sugar and make the body less sensitive to insulin, which sends blood glucose climbing. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T2#GNS222_U2_T2_h6)

question: A client with severe hypertension asks for oral contraceptive pills. What should the nurse do during the assessment?

options.A: Identify hypertension as a contraindication and discuss safer alternative methods
options.B: Prescribe the pills immediately because blood pressure does not matter
options.C: Refuse to check the client's blood pressure during the visit
options.D: Tell the client that birth control pills cure high blood pressure

explanation: Estrogen-containing pills can worsen high blood pressure and increase stroke risk, so nurses must screen for medical conditions and offer safer choices like progestin-only options. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h5)

question: What happens when illness or lack of water dries up the normal balance in the mouth?

options.A: Tooth enamel instantly repairs all of its own cavities
options.B: Bad bacteria multiply quickly and form dental plaque
options.C: The tongue changes its color to a bright lemon yellow
options.D: The salivary glands immediately shut down forever

explanation: When saliva drops due to sickness or dehydration, the protective shield weakens, letting nasty bacteria take over and build up as plaque. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T3#GNS112_U5_T3_h2)

question: What does a susceptible host represent in the chain of infection?

options.A: A medical instrument sterilized prior to a procedure
options.B: A person who lacks resistance to a specific pathogen
options.C: The physical surface where bacteria live and multiply
options.D: The specific pathway a virus uses to leave the body

explanation: A susceptible host is an individual whose immune system is weak or compromised enough to allow an infection to take hold. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which sociological theory suggests that older adults remain happier and healthier when they stay busy and socially involved?

options.A: Free radical theory
options.B: Activity theory
options.C: Disengagement theory
options.D: Wear-and-tear theory

explanation: Activity theory proposes that staying socially active and maintaining roles promotes well-being in older age. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which part of the brain acts like an alarm clock to keep us physically awake?

options.A: The peripheral nervous system
options.B: The spinal cord reflex arcs
options.C: The Ascending Reticular Activating System
options.D: The cerebellum and basal ganglia

explanation: Think of the ARAS as the brain's main power switch or alarm clock, sending constant wake-up signals from the brainstem to keep the cerebral cortex alert. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T6#GNS222_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why does scratching an itchy spot usually make the itch worse in the long run?

options.A: It numbs the skin permanently and causes local damage
options.B: It damages the skin cells, releasing more inflammatory chemicals

options.C: They are responsible for funding all local healthcare clinics
options.D: They write the country's penal and civil codes

explanation: Cultural and religious leaders shape how people think, making their support essential for real, lasting change in the community. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T9#GNS312_U1_T9_h7)

question: Which behavior do you typically see first in someone with Pick's disease?

options.A: Sudden tremors and rigidity in all four limbs
options.B: Inability to recognize familiar faces in mirrors
options.C: Loss of social inhibitions and personality changes
options.D: Complete loss of bladder and bowel control

explanation: Because the frontal lobe gets damaged, patients lose their 'social filter.' They might act very impulsively or say things they normally wouldn't, which is a classic sign to watch out for. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T6#GNS222_U4_T6_h3)

question: How can a nurse help a client who is struggling with transportation to a clinic appointment?

options.A: Connecting her with affordable clinic options or community support
options.B: Telling her that missing the appointment has no health consequences
options.C: Insisting that she buy a personal vehicle before discharge
options.D: Advising her to walk several miles alone in the hot afternoon sun

explanation: Practical problems like transport can stop mums from getting care. Helping them find nearby or affordable options makes a huge difference. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h7)

question: What serious heart condition can develop over time from chronic, untreated upper airway obstruction?

options.A: Aortic aneurysm
options.B: Cor pulmonale
options.C: Infective endocarditis
options.D: Mitral valve prolapse

explanation: When blocked airways starve the body of oxygen long-term, blood pressure in the lungs shoots up. This forces the right side of the heart to work overtime until it gets tired and fails (cor pulmonale). You've finished this set—take a bow! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h8)

question: Why do we follow a step-by-step reporting ladder for injection safety data?

options.A: It allows individual nurses to bypass hospital management
options.B: It prevents state and federal officers from seeing local clinic errors
options.C: It ensures that paperwork stays inside the hospital indefinitely
options.D: It allows data to be properly aggregated for national procurement planning

explanation: Spot on! Gathering data upward gives the country the accurate totals it needs to buy and distribute supplies for everyone. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h8)

question: Why is adolescent reproductive health such a vital focus for future wellness?

options.A: It accelerates physical growth beyond normal adult limits
options.B: It eliminates the need for adult healthcare screenings
options.C: It establishes a foundation for long-term reproductive capabilities and family health
options.D: It completely stops all future chronic illnesses in adulthood

explanation: Spot on! The health habits and experiences during the teenage years set the stage for a healthy reproductive life later on. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why must minor tranquilizers be reduced slowly (tapered) instead of stopping them all at once?

options.A: To ensure the prescription lasts until the next clinic visit
options.B: To allow the liver time to regenerate damaged cells
options.C: To prevent the patient from experiencing immediate weight gain
options.D: To prevent dangerous withdrawal symptoms like seizures

explanation: Stopping suddenly after the body has gotten used to the drug can cause severe rebound anxiety or even seizures. Safety first! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T4#GNS223_U6_T4_h6)

question: Which of these is a dangerous trap nurses should avoid when assessing patient pain?

options.A: Asking about the location of the discomfort
options.B: Believing that self-report is always the best method
options.C: Assuming a sleeping patient is completely free of pain
options.D: Using a 0-10 scale for adults with normal cognition

explanation: Never assume sleep means zero pain! Exhaustion can cause patients to drift off even when they are hurting badly. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T5#GNS321_U4_T5_h4)

question: A patient with large fibroids complains of constant tiredness, pale skin, and dizziness during her heavy periods. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Hormonal imbalance stopping ovulation completely
options.B: A sudden severe pelvic infection
options.C: Iron-deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss
options.D: Complete blockage of the cervix by scar tissue

explanation: Spot on! Losing a lot of blood month after month depletes the body's iron stores, leading to classic anemia symptoms like fatigue and paleness. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T19#GNS216_U5_T19_h3)

question: What do we mean by 'second victim syndrome' in healthcare?

options.A: A secondary illness caught by a patient while staying in the ward
options.B: Emotional trauma experienced by a clinician after being involved in an error
options.C: The legal penalty given to a hospital following a malpractice lawsuit
options.D: The family member who has to pay extra hospital bills for an injury

explanation: Nurses and doctors who go through a tough adverse event often carry deep emotional pain. We call them the second victims. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T8#GNS312_U5_T8_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard nursing duty when caring for patients on medication?

options.A: Changing the chemical composition of the drug in the IV bag
options.B: Evaluating lab results related to drug metabolism and excretion
options.C: Assessing the patient for unexpected adverse drug reactions
options.D: Checking vital signs to verify therapeutic effectiveness

explanation: Nurses administer and monitor, but altering drug formulas is strictly for pharmacists and manufacturers. You've got this! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T9#GNS125_U1_T9_h5)

question: What is the main goal of injection safety protocols in nursing?

options.A: To prevent harm to patients and protect healthcare workers
options.B: To ensure medications are absorbed faster by the body
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing new syringes
options.D: To speed up medication administration during busy shifts

explanation: Injection safety is all about keeping both sides safe—protecting the patient receiving the injection and keeping you, the nurse, safe from injuries and infections! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T4#GNS122_U4_T4_h1)

question: Your patient has a GI bleed. You notice their heart rate is rising and their blood pressure is falling. What does this most likely mean?

options.A: Normal recovery from bleeding
options.B: Developing hypovolemic shock
options.C: A sudden spike in blood sugar
options.D: Effective fluid volume overload

explanation: Brilliant deduction! When blood volume drops, the heart beats faster to try and compensate, but eventually blood pressure drops as shock sets in. You're thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h7)

question: A pregnant woman at 20 weeks ANC gets mosquito nets and iron supplements. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: To determine the exact genetic sex of the baby
options.B: To induce early labor in high-risk situations
options.C: To prevent malaria and treat or prevent anemia
options.D: To stop morning sickness during the first trimester

explanation: Malaria and low blood (anemia) are major risks in pregnancy, so nets and iron are standard lifesavers in our clinics. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h3)

question: A pregnant woman visits the ANC clinic for the first time at 28 weeks. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Check her vital signs, screen for infections, and check the baby's well-being
options.B: Schedule her for an elective sterilization procedure
options.C: Discharge her immediately because she came late
options.D: Tell her not to return until she goes into labor

explanation: Great clinical thinking! No matter when a woman starts ANC, your immediate duty as a nurse is to check her baseline status and screen for any pregnancy risks. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h3)

question: A state health board notices a sharp rise in infant mortality in a rural district through vital data. What action should they take first?

options.A: Increase taxes for citizens living in urban areas
options.B: Close all the primary schools in the affected region
options.C: Stop collecting birth data for the next five years
options.D: Direct more child health resources and immunisation teams to that district

explanation: When data highlights a specific problem area, health planners must channel targeted interventions directly to that community to save lives. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h7)

question: What type of acid-base imbalance builds up in the body during prolonged oxygen shortage?

options.A: Metabolic alkalosis
options.B: Respiratory acidosis
options.C: Metabolic acidosis
options.D: Respiratory alkalosis

explanation: Since anaerobic metabolism produces lactic acid, that acid buildup leads straight to metabolic acidosis. Great clinical connection to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T8#GNS123_U3_T8_h2)

question: An examiner is preparing to look at a patient's left eye using a direct ophthalmoscope. Which setup is correct?

options.A: Stand directly behind the patient and use both eyes at once
options.B: Rest the scope firmly against the bridge of the patient's nose
options.C: Hold the scope in the left hand and use the left eye
options.D: Hold the scope in the right hand and use the left eye

explanation: Using matching sides (left hand and left eye for the patient's left eye) allows the examiner to get close without colliding with the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is one of the common hurdles community health nurses face while working in many Nigerian settings?

options.A: Complete absence of public health problems to solve
options.B: Strict prohibition against working with local families
options.C: An overwhelming excess of modern medical equipment
options.D: Infrastructural deficits and resource constraints

explanation: You're doing amazing! Nigerian community nurses are true champions; they often navigate rough roads, limited supplies, and tough logistics to bring care to those who need it most. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T9#GNS225_U1_T9_h6)

question: What is the most immediate danger when a patient receives an incompatible blood transfusion?

options.A: Rapid growth of abnormal white blood cells in the bone marrow
options.B: Complete permanent loss of natural immunity to infections
options.C: Sudden permanent paralysis of the skeletal muscles
options.D: Destruction of red blood cells leading to kidney damage

explanation: Incompatible transfusions cause red blood cells to burst, releasing free hemoglobin that clogs and damages the kidneys. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h4)

question: How can you easily tell the difference between a vesicle and a bulla?

options.A: A vesicle contains pus while a bulla contains clear serum only
options.B: A vesicle appears on mucous membranes while a bulla appears on nails
options.C: A vesicle is smaller than 1 cm while a bulla is larger than 1 cm
options.D: A vesicle is solid and raised while a bulla is completely flat

explanation: Both are fluid-filled blisters! The only real difference is their size—bullae are just the bigger ones over 1 cm. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T8#GNS213_U5_T8_h2)

question: Keeping a hospital patient's call bell within easy reach is an action primarily aimed at meeting which type of need?

options.A: Love and belonging
options.B: Physiological rest
options.C: Self-actualization
options.D: Safety and security

explanation: A call bell gives the patient a way to call for help, satisfying their need for physical and environmental safety. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why are patients with swollen bellies (ascites) told to cut down on salt?

options.A: Salt makes the body hold onto water, worsening fluid in the belly
options.B: Sodium directly destroys liver cells if eaten in large amounts
options.C: Sodium prevents the body from absorbing water pills (diuretics)
options.D: High salt diets instantly trigger severe esophageal bleeding

explanation: Remember the golden rule: water follows salt! Keeping sodium low stops the kidneys from holding onto extra water, easing belly swelling. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the hardest, outermost protective layer of the tooth crown called?

options.A: Cementum
options.B: Pulp
options.C: Dentin
options.D: Enamel

explanation: Enamel covers the crown of the tooth and is the hardest substance in the human body, protecting the inner layers from damage. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do we encourage regular walking for patients with stable Peripheral Artery Disease?

options.A: It lowers the total volume of blood circulating in the body.
options.B: It immediately dissolves any deep vein blood clots in the legs.
options.C: It helps develop collateral blood vessels around blocked arteries.
options.D: It forces existing fatty plaque out through the capillary bed.

explanation: Exercise is amazing here! Gentle walking encourages the body to build tiny 'detour roads' (collateral vessels) to bypass the blocked main arteries. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T5#GNS123_U5_T5_h7)

question: Which of these is checked as part of a psychosocial health history?

options.A: Precise surgical incision healing progress
options.B: Coping mechanisms and daily stress management
options.C: Laboratory results from routine blood tests
options.D: Blood pressure readings taken over 24 hours

explanation: Correct! A psychosocial check looks at mental wellness, stress levels, and emotional support systems. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T3#GNS222_U3_T3_h7)

question: How do informal support networks—like caring neighbors—protect vulnerable people such as the elderly?

options.A: By taking over their legal and financial responsibilities completely
options.B: By replacing the need for professional nursing assessments
options.C: By moving all senior citizens into centralized government homes
options.D: By checking on them regularly and helping with daily tasks

explanation: Simple acts like checking in on grandma next door and helping with chores keep older folks safe, happy, and connected. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T5#GNS225_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why do first-generation antihistamines make patients so sleepy, while newer ones usually do not?

options.A: Second-generation drugs are broken down entirely in the stomach.
options.B: First-generation drugs cross the blood-brain barrier easily.
options.C: First-generation drugs reduce blood pressure too quickly.
options.D: Second-generation drugs contain natural caffeine additives.

explanation: Exactly! Because they easily slip into the central nervous system, first-gen drugs cause that heavy drowsiness we all know. Newer drugs are designed to stay out of the brain. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T8#GNS215_U6_T8_h2)

question: Where should a used injection needle go immediately after you give an injection?

options.A: Into a puncture-resistant safety box at the point of use
options.B: Onto a metal tray to be collected at the end of the shift
options.C: Into the general black waste bin for municipal pickup
options.D: Back into its original plastic packaging for storage

explanation: Sharps go straight into a safety box right where you performed the procedure. Never walk around with a naked needle looking for a bin! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h7)

question: Which of these heart rhythms needs an immediate emergency shock?

options.A: Sinus Bradycardia
options.B: Ventricular Fibrillation
options.C: Asystole
options.D: Pulseless Electrical Activity

explanation: Ventricular Fibrillation (VF) is a shockable rhythm because the heart still has wild electrical activity that a shock can clear. Flatlines (asystole) need chest compressions and meds, not shocks! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T17#GNS213_U1_T17_h1)

question: What does the term 'deprescribing' mean in clinical practice?

options.A: Writing a brand new prescription after a patient loses their drug chart
options.B: Increasing the dosage strength of a drug to make it work much faster
options.C: Switching a patient from tablets to intravenous injections in the ward
options.D: The planned, supervised process of stopping or reducing unnecessary medications

explanation: Deprescribing isn't abandoning a patient—it's a clever, safe way to trim down unnecessary pills and reduce side effects under medical guidance. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T9#GNS215_U1_T9_h5)

question: What test is mainly used to check for a broken bone after a bad joint injury?

options.A: Urinalysis
options.B: Electrocardiogram
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: X-ray imaging

explanation: An X-ray gives a clear picture of the bones, helping doctors easily rule out a fracture when a patient comes in with severe trauma. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T9#GNS222_U1_T9_h3)

question: A patient asks when is the best time to take her ibuprofen for menstrual cramps. What should the nurse say?

options.A: Take it every morning for the entire month regardless of symptoms
options.B: Take the medication only after your menstrual bleeding stops
options.C: Wait until the pain becomes unbearable before taking any pill
options.D: Take it at the very start of your period or when pain begins

explanation: Well done! NSAIDs work best when taken early, before prostaglandins have a chance to build up and cause severe pain. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h7)

question: Which patients should receive Standard Precautions?

options.A: Every patient in the healthcare setting
options.B: Only patients with weak immune systems
options.C: Only patients admitted to the emergency room
options.D: Only patients with confirmed infections

explanation: Always treat every patient with Standard Precautions! We treat everyone as if they could carry an infection, keeping both them and us safe. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h3)

question: Which symptom is a major red flag for Meniere's disease?

options.A: Sudden complete ear pain
options.B: Bleeding from the ear canal
options.C: Purulent ear discharge
options.D: Episodic vertigo

explanation: Spot on! Meniere's disease causes sudden, severe spells of spinning dizziness (vertigo), along with ringing in the ears and hearing changes. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T5#GNS311_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which part of the eye provides the majority of its light-focusing power?

options.A: The iris
options.B: The retina
options.C: The lens
options.D: The cornea

explanation: The cornea is the clear front surface of the eye that handles most of the heavy lifting when it comes to bending and focusing incoming light. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T3#GNS311_U3_T3_h1)

question: When should you refer a reproductive health patient to a specialist counselor?

options.A: When emotional distress exceeds basic supportive nursing care
options.B: Whenever the patient asks what medication they are taking
options.C: Only after the patient has completed all surgical treatments
options.D: Before the nurse performs any physical assessment

explanation: Spot on! While you provide great initial comfort, deep or complex emotional distress is best handled by mental health specialists. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T14#GNS311_U1_T14_h7)

question: A community nurse needs official guidelines to start a new polio vaccine drive. Where is the best place to check first?

options.A: International fashion magazines
options.B: Private pharmaceutical marketing flyers
options.C: Local hospital cafeteria menus
options.D: National public health agency directives

explanation: Exactly! National health agencies provide the official schedules and steps that community health workers rely on for immunization campaigns. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T6#GNS112_U1_T6_h2)

question: How should you write entries in a permanent clinic register to keep records safe and professional?

options.A: In shorthand code that only the head nurse understands
options.B: Neatly in ink without unauthorized erasures
options.C: In pencil so mistakes can be easily rubbed out
options.D: Using colored markers to make pages look bright

explanation: Permanent registers need ink to prevent any tampering. If you make a mistake, simply cross it out cleanly rather than erasing it! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T13#GNS225_U2_T13_h4)

question: Which of these is a classic sign that a patient with diarrhoea is starting to get dehydrated?

options.A: Swelling in both lower legs and ankles
options.B: Dry mucous membranes and poor skin turgor
options.C: Excessive production of clear saliva
options.D: Increased blood pressure and flushed skin

explanation: When body fluid drops, tissues lose their bounce and moisture. Look out for a sticky dry mouth and skin that takes a moment to snap back when pinched! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of clamping and occluding instruments?

options.A: To compress blood vessels and stop bleeding
options.B: To hold wound edges open for better visibility
options.C: To cut through tough bone and cartilage
options.D: To stitch the skin closed at the end of surgery

explanation: Clamping tools like hemostats squeeze bleeding vessels shut to maintain a clear field of vision during the procedure. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h2)

question: How do simple antacids neutralize extra stomach acid without using cell receptors?

options.A: Through direct chemical neutralization
options.B: By binding to specialized membrane enzymes
options.C: By blocking hormone production in the liver
options.D: Through osmotic drawing of fluid into cells

explanation: Not all drugs need receptors! Antacids simply mix with the stomach acid in a direct chemical reaction to calm things down right away. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T5#GNS125_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why should nurses tell patients not to chew gum or smoke while fasting for this test?

options.A: They mess up the laboratory machine used to spin blood
options.B: They can trigger digestion and change the blood sugar results
options.C: They cause severe dehydration that collapses arm veins
options.D: They immediately destroy all red blood cells in the body

explanation: Even tiny actions like chewing gum can trick the body into releasing insulin, throwing off the test results. Patient instructions matter! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T18#GNS222_U2_T18_h3)

question: A patient is pacing the ward rapidly, breathing fast, and speaking in a frantic rush. What should you do first?

options.A: Administer a strong oral stimulant to boost their energy.
options.B: Move the patient to a quiet area and speak in a calm, reassuring tone.
options.C: Leave the patient alone until they calm down on their own.
options.D: Ask the patient to sit down and fill out a detailed anxiety questionnaire.

explanation: Lowering the noise and distractions around the patient—paired with your own calm presence—does wonders to bring their anxiety down. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T10#GNS123_U3_T10_h7)

question: Why might two people taking the exact same dose of cough syrup react completely differently?

options.A: The color of the syrup changes how fast the stomach digests it.
options.B: Different brands use completely different active ingredients.
options.C: The time of day changes the weight of the medication.
options.D: Genetic differences in liver enzymes affect drug breakdown rates.

explanation: We all process drugs at our own pace because of our unique liver enzymes (like CYP2D6)! One person might clear it fast, while another feels it much longer. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T1#GNS223_U2_T1_h4)

question: When should you definitely NOT perform a rectal washout?

options.A: A stable history of controlled high blood pressure
options.B: Temporary loss of appetite for two days
options.C: Recent bowel surgery with an active anastomosis
options.D: Mild chronic constipation in an elderly adult

explanation: Never force fluid into a fresh surgical connection (anastomosis)! The pressure could cause it to break open, leading to dangerous leaks. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h3)

question: Which patient has the highest risk of developing cholesterol gallstones?

options.A: An elderly male who exercises daily and eats low-fat meals
options.B: An adolescent male eating a high-protein diet
options.C: A young adult female with a low body mass index
options.D: A middle-aged female who lost weight very rapidly

explanation: Great thinking! Being female, middle-aged, and undergoing rapid weight loss are classic risk factors due to hormonal shifts and bile changes. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why is waiting for low blood pressure a risky way to spot early internal bleeding in a young adult?

options.A: Strong compensatory mechanisms keep blood pressure normal until shock is severe
options.B: Internal bleeding actually makes blood pressure rise first
options.C: Young adults never get low blood pressure
options.D: Cuffs cannot measure pressure accurately during shock

explanation: Young bodies work overtime to hide blood loss by tightening blood vessels and racing the heart, so blood pressure can stay normal even when they're in trouble. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T4#GNS221_U3_T4_h4)

question: Where does most of the gas in our digestive tract actually come from?

options.A: Drinking carbonated beverages and kidney filtration
options.B: Swallowed air and bacterial fermentation in the colon
options.C: Direct diffusion from the bloodstream and liver bile
options.D: Chemical reactions in the stomach acid and saliva

explanation: Think about it two ways: air we swallow when eating or talking, and the bacteria in our gut breaking down food. Simple and natural! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T10#GNS212_U1_T10_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a sign of low calcium levels in the blood?

options.A: Nerve twitching and muscle spasms
options.B: Increased neuromuscular irritability
options.C: Numbness around the mouth
options.D: Increased muscle strength and bulk

explanation: You got it! Low calcium makes nerves super jumpy (causing tingles and spasms), but it doesn't magically build bigger muscles. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T7#GNS123_U3_T7_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a physical problem caused by long-term, unmanaged stress?

options.A: Amplified perception of physical pain
options.B: Exacerbation of chronic hypertension
options.C: Improved gastrointestinal absorption of all nutrients
options.D: Delayed wound healing and tissue repair

explanation: Stress actually messes with digestion and reduces nutrient absorption—it definitely doesn't improve your gut health! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h8)

question: Which of the following is evaluated when assessing the sensory system during a neurological exam?

options.A: Light touch and pain perception
options.B: Muscle bulk and involuntary twitching
options.C: Deep tendon reflex hammer response
options.D: Level of orientation to time and place

explanation: Sensory evaluations focus on how well the patient perceives external stimuli like touch, pain, and vibration. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is getting the family involved so important when helping a teen recover from digital addiction?

options.A: Household routines, communication styles, and boundaries heavily influence recovery
options.B: Parents are legally required to operate the patient's smartphone for them
options.C: It prevents the teenager from ever leaving the family home again
options.D: Family members are the only people allowed to prescribe counseling medication

explanation: Healing doesn't happen in a vacuum. Since home life shapes daily habits, the whole family working together makes a massive difference in recovery. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T14#GNS312_U3_T14_h7)

question: What is the most common cause of primary hyperparathyroidism?

options.A: Severe dietary calcium deficiency
options.B: Chronic inflammation of the thyroid
options.C: Autoimmune destruction of the glands
options.D: A benign parathyroid adenoma

explanation: Most of the time, primary hyperparathyroidism is caused by a single non-cancerous (benign) growth or adenoma on one of the parathyroid glands. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T11#GNS222_U2_T11_h3)

question: What complication is a patient most at risk for if they receive many blood transfusions over several years?

options.A: Acute hemolytic shock
options.B: Immediate anaphylaxis
options.C: Bacterial sepsis
options.D: Iron overload

explanation: Our bodies are great at using iron, but terrible at getting rid of excess iron! Over years of multiple transfusions, that extra iron starts piling up in vital organs like the liver and heart. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T12#GNS311_U2_T12_h6)

question: The doctor orders Paracetamol 500 mg. Pharmacy sends Paracetamol scored tablets of 250 mg each. How many tablets will you give?

options.A: 1 tablet
options.B: 0.5 tablets
options.C: 4 tablets
options.D: 2 tablets

question: Why do doctors and nurses prefer ultrasound when a patient needs repeated scans over a short time?

options.A: it does not use harmful ionizing radiation
options.B: It is totally painless and needs no practice
options.C: It gives a much clearer view of bones than a CT scan
options.D: It completely replaces the need for blood tests

explanation: Because it lacks harmful radiation, ultrasound is super safe and can be repeated as many times as needed to monitor healing. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why is keeping an eye on chronic health conditions so important during post-abortion care?

options.A: It guarantees immediate fertility restoration
options.B: It prevents minor issues from becoming emergencies
options.C: It eliminates the need for pain medication
options.D: It reduces hospital administrative costs

explanation: Spotting and managing chronic diseases early stops them from flaring up and getting worse during a time when the body is under physical stress. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T017#GNS226_U5_T017_h1)

question: What metabolic issue is closely linked to high male hormone levels in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)?

options.A: Insulin resistance
options.B: Iron deficiency
options.C: Taking too much Vitamin C
options.D: Eating too much salt

explanation: Spot on! When the body shows insulin resistance, insulin levels rise, which triggers the ovaries to pump out extra androgens. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why is Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) so popular during community outreaches and emergencies?

question: Which of these is a healthy, adaptive way for a patient to cope with a chronic illness?

question: Which patient position is best for chest tube insertion to help expand the lung and make the area easy to reach?

question: What is the main reason nurses use functional assessment tools in rehab?

question: Why must blood-soaked dressings be treated as hazardous infectious waste?

question: Which skin gland secretes an oily substance called sebum?

question: A patient who had a laparoscopic tubal ligation two hours ago complains of sharp pain in her right shoulder. What is the best nursing action?

question: Which mental health challenge is very common among young brides who are cut off from their friends?

options.A: Bipolar manic episodes
options.B: Schizophrenic hallucinations
options.C: Depression and anxiety
options.D: Obsessive compulsive rituals

question: Why are open fractures so much more likely to cause bone infections than closed fractures?

options.C: Broken skin allows external bacteria direct access to the bone tissue.

question: What does an Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) test actually measure?

options.C: How much oxygen is trapped in the toe capillaries

question: What is the main physical state behind chronic insomnia?

options.A: Hyperarousal
options.B: Parasympathetic dominance
options.C: Hypoglycemia
options.D: Metabolic slowdown

question: Which lab results are most important for a nurse to watch when caring for a patient with a bleeding disorder?

options.A: Liver enzymes and serum creatinine levels

options.C: Platelet count and coagulation profiles
options.D: White blood cell differential and blood cultures

question: A teenager avoids emergency contraception because she believes it causes permanent infertility. What type of barrier is this?

explanation: Myths and false beliefs about side effects are psychological barriers rooted in misinformation. Gentle education goes a long way here. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T10#GNS312_U3_T10_h2)

question: Which question type is best for encouraging a patient to tell their story in their own words?

options.A: Closed-ended questions
options.B: Multiple-choice questions
options.C: Leading questions
options.D: Open-ended questions

explanation: Open-ended questions allow patients to elaborate freely without limiting their responses to a single word. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h2)

question: What room-air oxygen saturation level helps nurses classify a patient's COVID-19 illness as severe?

question: Which specific cells in the testes are responsible for making testosterone?

question: Why do we take time to spot and manage occupational hazards right inside the operating room?

question: Why can psychological abuse be just as damaging as physical abuse?

options.C: It is easily diagnosed through standard blood and urine tests

question: A patient has osteoarthritis in their knee. Which symptom are they most likely to feel?

options.C: Rapid lengthening of the affected limb over weeks
options.D: Pain and stiffness that worsens with physical activity

question: Why is occupational therapy so helpful for patients with chronic joint disorders?

options.B: It teaches energy-conservation techniques and assistive devices
options.C: It cures the underlying autoimmune malfunction
options.D: It prescribes high-dose corticosteroid injections

question: An infusion pump starts beeping with a 'downstream occlusion' alarm. What should you check first?

question: When does a nurse actually begin assessing a client's respiratory status?

options.D: The moment the nurse first sees the client

question: A patient complains of constant dizziness and trouble keeping their balance. Which part of the ear is likely involved?

options.A: External ear canal
options.B: Auditory ossicles
options.C: Tympanic membrane
options.D: Semicircular canals

question: What is the most important instruction for a patient going home with oral antibiotics for salpingitis?

question: Why do we keep a patient with a suspected spinal injury flat on a hard board?

question: What is the biggest benefit of nurses and physical therapists working closely together?

question: A nurse is preparing to start a blood transfusion for an adult patient. Which intravenous solution should be used to prime the Y-tubing?

options.D: Lactated Ringer's solution

question: You visit a patient and find an empty fridge and unpaid bills piling up. What should this tell you?

options.C: A normal metabolic adaptation to advanced aging

question: In the chain of infection, what do we call the cozy home base where a germ lives, grows, and multiplies?

question: Which organ is in the greatest danger during a paracetamol overdose?

question: What is the main difference between an orthosis and a prosthesis?

question: What is a major lung hazard when giving activated charcoal to a patient by mouth?

question: Why are grieving individuals more prone to catching frequent colds or infections?

question: What does the term 'groupnorms' mean in a nursing unit?

question: Why is it important to test blood sugar while a patient is fasting?

question: Why must nurses always ask patients if they are taking traditional or herbal remedies along with prescribed drugs?

question: A 65-year-old worker with long-term chemical exposure comes in with tiredness. Which background factor makes you suspect a blood issue?

question: Why don't doctors do throat swabs for every person who walks in with a mild cold?

question: How can you, as a bedside nurse, help improve injection safety standards in your clinic?

question: What does the glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) test measure in a client?

question: What is the single most important infection control habit in maternity care?

question: What would you expect to see in a patient experiencing acute low calcium (hypocalcemia) due to a parathyroid problem?

question: Why do DRF programs love buying drugs by their generic names?

question: How often should an antenatal clinic see a pregnant woman with sickle cell disease during her first two trimesters?

question: A nurse is changing a dressing on a large surgical abdominal wound. What is the primary reason for using sterile instruments and supplies?

options.C: To stop the patient from feeling pain during the procedure

question: A patient has an apical pulse of 110 bpm, but a radial pulse of only 84 bpm. What does this gap mean?

question: Why does a baby with Tetralogy of Fallot sometimes turn very blue when crying?

question: A client says she still takes her birth control pill every day, but admits she forgets it at least three times a week. How would you describe this?

question: What does the 'T' stand for in the TNM cancer staging system?

question: Why must a National Drug Policy tie in closely with the National Health Policy?

question: What is the main goal of hormone therapy in certain cancers?

question: How do doctors usually confirm a diagnosis of Korsakoff syndrome?

question: What is the best way to help an awake, intubated patient communicate with you?

question: Which agency is primarily responsible for regulating drugs in Nigeria?

question: What is the main job of the Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL)?

options.D: To calculate the exact number of calories burned during rest

explanation: Think of the UL as a safety warning light. It tells us the highest amount of a nutrient a person can take before it starts causing harm, especially from supplements. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h2)

question: What kind of sound do you usually hear when tapping (percussing) over an area filled with fluid like a pleural effusion?

options.A: Vesicular resonance
options.B: Hyperresonance
options.C: Dullness
options.D: Tympany

explanation: Fluid dampens the vibration, giving a flat, dull sound instead of a hollow ring. Keep practicing your physical assessment skills—they get easier every day! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T7#GNS213_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is the main job of vitamin D made in the skin?

options.A: Preventing ultraviolet radiation damage to cells
options.B: Eliminating excess urea through sweat glands
options.C: Assisting with calcium absorption in the body
options.D: Regulating core body temperature during a fever

explanation: Great job! Sunlight on the skin helps create vitamin D, which your body needs to properly absorb calcium for strong bones and teeth. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h1)

question: Why do people often get confused by the word 'stress' in stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: They believe it is caused by mental exhaustion
options.B: They assume it only happens during high-intensity sports
options.C: They confuse it with neurological distress
options.D: They think it relates to emotional anxiety rather than physical pressure

explanation: It's an easy mix-up! In this case, 'stress' means physical force or pressure on your organs, not emotional stress or worry. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h1)

question: How is Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) viewed under international human rights law?

options.A: An acceptable alternative traditional medicine practice
options.B: A mandatory cultural initiation rite for minors
options.C: A violation of human rights and bodily integrity
options.D: A minor surgical procedure with health benefits

explanation: Spot on! Global human rights laws recognize FGM as an act of violence that strips women and children of their fundamental right to physical safety and health. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T5#GNS225_U6_T5_h1)

question: What is the primary definition of the rectal route of drug administration?

options.A: Inhaling drug vapors directly into the lungs
options.B: Applying medicated cream onto the outer skin
options.C: Swallowing medicine with a large glass of water
options.D: Inserting medication directly into the rectum

explanation: The rectal route simply means placing a drug directly into the rectal cavity for local or systemic effects. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h1)

question: How is grief different from bereavement?

options.A: Grief is the internal emotional response, while bereavement is the overall state of deprivation after a loss
options.B: Grief is a public ceremony, whereas bereavement is a private medical diagnosis
options.C: Grief only happens after sudden trauma, while bereavement occurs exclusively in chronic illnesses
options.D: Grief involves physical pain only, while bereavement involves purely spiritual distress

explanation: Exactly right! Grief is the heavy emotional feeling inside, while bereavement is the broader period of experiencing the loss of someone close to you. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T9#GNS321_U4_T9_h2)

question: What is the main goal of mobile medical outreaches for persons with disabilities in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: To gather statistical research data without providing direct care
options.B: To replace all permanent primary healthcare clinics in the country
options.C: To conduct advanced surgical operations in local village squares
options.D: To bring essential healthcare services and assistive devices closer to underserved populations

explanation: Outreach brings care right to the doorsteps of people who can't easily travel to big city hospitals. Vital work for community health! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T15#GNS225_U5_T15_h7)

question: Which sign during a thoracocentesis might indicate a vasovagal reaction?

options.A: Dizziness, sweating, and a sudden drop in heart rate
options.B: A rapid spike in blood pressure and excessive talking
options.C: Sudden redness and warmth spreading over the face
options.D: An intense urge to cough continuously for ten minutes

explanation: Pain, anxiety, or fluid shifts can trigger a vasovagal response, causing low heart rate, low blood pressure, and dizziness. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h5)

question: What is the name of the smooth inner lining of a joint capsule that gets inflamed in many rheumatic disorders?

options.A: Endosteum
options.B: Synovium
options.C: Periosteum
options.D: Myocardium

explanation: The synovium is the delicate membrane lining our joints. When inflammatory conditions flare up, this lining is usually the main target of the immune response. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T12#GNS222_U1_T12_h2)

question: Why do nurses do a baseline neurologic assessment when a patient is first admitted?

options.A: To determine the exact cost of hospital care
options.B: To replace the need for diagnostic imaging scans
options.C: To cure underlying nerve cell damage
options.D: To detect any changes in patient status over time

explanation: Think of a baseline as your starting snapshot! It gives you a reference point so if the patient's condition changes later, you can spot it right away. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T20#GNS222_U3_T20_h1)

question: Why can taking regular doses of NSAIDs (like ibuprofen) lead to stomach ulcers?

options.A: They block protective chemicals (prostaglandins) that help build stomach mucus
options.B: They paralyze the smooth muscles responsible for stomach movement
options.C: They directly increase the total amount of acid in your stomach
options.D: They force the lower esophageal sphincter to stay wide open all day

explanation: NSAIDs block helpful prostaglandins, which strips away your stomach's natural mucus and bicarbonate armor, leaving the tissue vulnerable to acid damage. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h2)

question: Why is self-medication so common across Nigeria?

options.A: Standard hospitals rarely stock basic pain relief tablets
options.B: People prefer reading package leaflets over talking to doctors
options.C: Hospital queues, costs, and easy access to open-air drug markets drive the practice
options.D: The government mandates that every citizen treat themselves first

explanation: You got it! Long wait times at clinics and financial constraints often push people to easily accessible informal drug vendors instead. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the main job of Regulatory T-cells (T-regs)?

options.A: To engulf large cellular debris via phagocytosis in tissues
options.B: To suppress excessive immune responses and prevent autoimmunity
options.C: To form physical barriers on mucosal and skin surfaces
options.D: To produce high affinity antibodies against foreign bacteria

explanation: Well done! T-regs act like peacekeepers, calming down the immune system after a fight so it doesn't accidentally attack healthy body tissue. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h7)

question: Which patient group requires the greatest caution when taking anticholinergic medications?

options.A: Older adult patients
options.B: Young children with fevers
options.C: Pregnant women in their first trimester
options.D: Athletes with muscle sprains

explanation: Older adults are much more sensitive to side effects like confusion, constipation, and urinary retention, increasing complication risks. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T6#GNS223_U5_T6_h6)

question: Why might a nurse manager sometimes fail to use the most theoretically perfect solution to a problem?

options.A: Theory never has any connection to real-world nursing
options.B: Hospital policy forbids the use of logic in management
options.C: Staff members always refuse to do any work at all
options.D: Power dynamics and institutional policies create practical limits

explanation: In the real hospital environment, politics, hospital policies, and power struggles often force managers to find practical compromises. [learn more](GST321_U1_T8#GST321_U1_T8_h5)
